tool_name: Import and Migration UX (Cross-tool Survey, 2025-2026) — covering Jira (new import experience + JCMA), Linear (in-product importers + CLI), ClickUp (Jira/Asana/Trello importers), Asana (CSV + Jira), monday.com (CSV + integrations), Notion (Monday.com importer beta), Targetprocess (CSV + ADM + Jira sync), Plane (multi-tool importers), Planview Hub (Rally/Targetprocess/Jira sync), OpsHub / Kovair / Deviniti / ServiceRocket (services-led migration vendors), ServiceNow EAP (Dec 2025 Jira integration)
target_user: Bimodal. Small/medium migrations (<10k items, single project): self-service by an admin or power user using built-in CSV importers and native connectors. Large enterprise migrations (50k+ items, multi-project, custom fields, history preservation): services engagement near-universal — OpsHub, Kovair, Deviniti, ServiceRocket, Praecipio, Isos, SPK & Associates all market dedicated migration services. Even with vendor-built tools (Atlassian JCMA, Planview Hub), enterprise migrations are typically led by a partner SI. ServiceNow EAP migrations to/from Jira require admin role on both sides plus partner involvement at enterprise scale.
setup_time_estimate: Self-service CSV import: minutes to hours per project depending on field mapping iteration. Linear in-product Jira importer: hours for a typical 1–5k issue migration. Jira's new import experience: 'minutes' for small CSV, hours-to-days for large multi-project imports. Real-world enterprise: cotera.co reported a 2,000-issue Jira→Linear migration as a multi-day effort with data-model gaps surfacing. OpsHub / Kovair Rally→Jira enterprise migrations: typically 4–12 weeks with zero-downtime requirements. ServiceNow EAP ↔ Jira via Dec 2025 OOTB integration: 'guided setup' but no published time benchmarks. [uncertain] on average time-to-complete benchmarks across vendors.
onboarding_wizard: Jira's new CSV import wizard (2024–2025) is the current best-in-class native flow: upload CSV → auto-detect date format → auto-map columns to fields by name match → review unmapped → choose project (new or existing) → map issue types and hierarchy (Issue ID + Parent for Epic→Story→Subtask) → preview → import. Linear in-product importer (Jira/Asana/Shortcut/Trello/GitHub/CSV) is similarly stepped, with bulk-delete-import as an undo. Atlassian JCMA: project-by-project assessment → app compatibility check → user/group mapping → run migration → verify. ClickUp importers: source-tool OAuth → choose workspaces/projects → field mapping → import. Plane: multi-source connectors with a wizard per source. No vendor yet ships an AI-assisted import wizard that proposes schema mappings.
template_library: Migration 'templates' here means saved mapping configurations and pre-built schema translators. Jira's new import experience now supports reusable mapping configurations across imports. Linear ships opinionated defaults rather than mapping templates. OpsHub and Kovair ship pre-built schema mappers for Rally→Jira, Rally→ADO, Jira→ADO etc. as their core product. Targetprocess ATP↔ADM (Apptio Data Management) ships pre-built integrations to other Apptio products. Atlassian Marketplace hosts community-shared CSV templates for common migrations. [uncertain] on whether mapping templates are shareable across orgs in any vendor.
ai_assisted_setup: Near-zero AI in migration UX as of May 2026 — the standout gap in the market. Heuristic auto-mapping (Jira: match CSV column name to Jira field name, detect date format) is the ceiling. No vendor ships AI that reads a foreign schema and proposes a target hierarchy with confidence scores. No vendor ships AI that summarizes a migration's quality ('these 47 epics map cleanly; these 12 stories have custom fields with no obvious target — review needed'). This is the single biggest opportunity in agile-tool migration UX. [uncertain] on private betas — Atlassian Rovo and ClickUp Brain could plausibly add this in 2026 but neither is shipping it.
hierarchy_config: Hierarchy mapping is the hardest part of every migration and the place where services engagements get expensive. Jira's new importer now exposes Issue ID + Parent columns for Epic→Story→Subtask preservation, and Premium/Enterprise tiers add custom hierarchy levels above Epic. Linear's hierarchy (Initiative→Project→Issue→Sub-issue) is fixed and shallower than Jira/Rally, causing forced flattening during Jira→Linear migrations — cotera.co's review of 2,000-issue migration explicitly cited this. Rally→Jira: Rally's Portfolio Items (Theme→Initiative→Feature) map to Jira's custom hierarchy levels, requires Premium/Enterprise; Rally Test Cases map to Zephyr/Xray (separate add-on). SAFe-level hierarchies (Portfolio→Epic→Capability→Feature→Story) are not natively preserved by any cross-tool CSV import — requires services or specialist sync tools (Planview Hub, OpsHub).
multi_team_setup: Multi-team migrations are where self-service collapses and services take over. Jira's new importer can chain multiple project imports but team/user mapping at scale (100+ users, multiple AD groups) is admin-heavy. Atlassian JCMA explicitly does not bulk-delete users or groups, and bulk operations require paid third-party apps — a known pain point. Linear scales by team-per-team importer runs; no single 'org-level' migration wizard. ServiceNow EAP scaling involves ART/Program-level config that the OOTB Dec 2025 Jira integration handles project-by-project. Enterprise migrations of 50+ teams universally involve partner services to script user/group mapping, custom field reconciliation, and sprint history reconstruction.
admin_dependency: Heavy. Jira CSV import: org admin, site admin, or Jira admin required for the new import experience (team-managed business spaces are an exception). Atlassian JCMA: admin on both source and destination. Linear importer: workspace admin. ClickUp importers: workspace admin or owner. ServiceNow EAP-Jira integration: admin on both, plus ServiceNow plugin install. The boundary between admin and user is sharper in migration than anywhere else — almost nothing can be done by a non-admin. Self-service migration requires the team lead to *be* the admin (common in startups) or to wait on IT (common in enterprise).
permissions_model: Permission preservation across migration is generally manual. Jira's importer maps users by email and creates missing users on destination; group/role assignment is post-import. Linear's importer creates issues under the importing user's identity unless a separate user-mapping step is run via CLI. Rally→Jira tools (OpsHub, Kovair) preserve assignee history but typically not permission roles — those are re-applied based on destination policy. ServiceNow EAP uses its native role model post-migration. No tool ships AI that recommends a destination permission model based on source patterns.
import_capabilities: Survey of native importers as of May 2026: Jira — CSV, Asana (new in 2024), monday.com (new in 2024), Trello, Linear (new in 2025), JCMA for Jira-to-Jira. Linear — Jira, Asana, Shortcut, Trello, GitHub Issues, CSV, plus CLI. ClickUp — Jira, Asana, Trello, Monday, Wrike, Basecamp, CSV. Asana — CSV, Jira, Trello, Smartsheet, Wrike. monday.com — CSV, Excel, Trello, Asana, Jira. Notion — Asana, Trello, Evernote, CSV, Monday.com (beta 2025). Plane — Jira, Linear, Asana, ClickUp, Monday, CSV. Targetprocess — CSV, ADM, native Jira sync (bidirectional). ServiceNow EAP — Jira (OOTB Dec 2025), Azure DevOps (separate integration). Field mapping quality varies wildly: simple (title, description, status, assignee) is universally well-mapped; custom fields, attachments, comments, history, sprint state, and workflow transitions are where tools diverge sharply. Linear retains comments/attachments via in-product importer better than CSV. Jira's new importer is one of the most complete native importers. CSV remains the universal fallback but loses comments and attachments.
migration_story: Best-in-class native migration UX as of 2025–2026: (1) Linear's in-product Jira importer — praised for getting titles/descriptions/assignees/status across cleanly, but flattens Jira hierarchy and loses sprint state (cotera.co 2,000-issue review). (2) Jira's new import experience — best-in-class for inbound migrations from Asana/monday/Linear/Trello/CSV; clear mapping UI, auto-date-detection. (3) Notion's Monday.com importer (beta 2025) — clean OAuth flow, board-level granularity. Worst patterns: bulk user/group delete in Atlassian JCMA (paid third-party app needed); workflow state mapping in any Rally→anything migration (requires services). Services-led: Rally→Jira via OpsHub, Kovair, Deviniti, Praecipio, Isos is the default at enterprise scale. ServiceNow EAP's Dec 2025 OOTB Jira integration is positioned as an interim two-step approach with a bidirectional native integration on the roadmap; sprints cannot be synchronized in the interim — a meaningful limitation. Real user verdict (Atlassian community, 2024–2025): 'migration effort amounts to years worth of server admin/maintenance.' Pattern across reviews: native tools handle <5k items reasonably; >50k items effectively requires services. Standout reduction-of-human-dependency: Plane's AI-positioned multi-source importer and Linear's bulk-undo (delete entire import in one click) are the two most user-empowering features in shipping products.
vcs_integration_setup: Post-migration VCS reconnection is typically a separate, manual step in every tool — branches and PRs do not migrate, only references. Linear's GitHub/GitLab integration reconnects by repo and learns the team's branch naming. Jira's DevOps connection survives migration if the same GitHub org is connected on the destination. ClickUp, Asana, Monday all require re-OAuth post-migration. ServiceNow EAP's VCS state model is newer and not directly migratable from Jira DevOps. No tool ships AI that re-maps PR/commit links from old issue IDs to new issue IDs automatically — this is manual or scripted today. [uncertain] on whether OpsHub/Kovair migration tools preserve VCS links — partial preservation claimed in OpsHub Rally→ADO case studies.
slack_notifications_setup: Slack rules are not migrated by any tool — users must reinstall the destination's Slack app and rebuild notification rules. This is universally a post-migration manual step and a common complaint in G2 reviews ('we migrated the data but lost two weeks of Slack noise rebuilding routing'). Slack's own AI Workflow Builder (2025) could in principle let users describe their old routing rules in natural language to rebuild, but no PM tool ships a tight integration for this. Net: Slack rebuild is a hidden migration cost.
first_impression_ux: First-run of the import wizard sets the tone for the entire migration. Best: Linear and Jira's new importer both open with a tool picker, clear OAuth-or-CSV branching, and a sample preview before commit. Notion's Monday.com importer (beta) shows board thumbnails. Plane shows source-tool icons with one-click connection. Worst: Atlassian JCMA's project-by-project flow with cryptic 'app assessment' screens (Atlassian community complaints, 2024–2025) and a 'choose migration stage' control that is widely reported as misleading. Sample-data preview before commit is the single highest-impact UX feature here and is missing in most enterprise tools.
time_to_value: Migration time-to-value is measured in 'when can my team actually start working in the new tool with all their context?' For small migrations (<5k items, single team) using Linear/Jira/ClickUp native importers: hours to a day. For enterprise (multi-project, custom fields, history): weeks to months including UAT. The 'we moved from Jira to X over a weekend' claim in vendor marketing is generally only achievable for teams under 1k items with minimal custom fields. Self-service tier ceiling appears to be ~5–10k items; above that, services are pragmatically required regardless of vendor marketing.
setup_complaints: Top complaints from G2, Atlassian community, Reddit r/projectmanagement, and partner blogs (2024–2026): (1) 'Hierarchy flattening on Jira→Linear' — Linear's shallower model loses Epic→Story→Subtask depth (cotera.co, 2025). (2) 'Custom fields don't survive CSV' — universal across all tools; CSV import handles built-in fields well, custom fields require manual creation first then re-mapping. (3) 'Sprint history doesn't migrate' — ServiceNow EAP-Jira Dec 2025 integration explicitly excludes sprints; Rally→Jira tools also lose iteration history without paid add-ons. (4) 'Attachments and comments lost on CSV' — fundamental CSV limitation; native importers (Linear's Jira importer) handle this better. (5) 'Misleading import-stage controls in JCMA' — Atlassian community 2024. (6) 'No undo' — except Linear (bulk-delete-import). (7) 'Field mapping screen lacks issue-type field' (Atlassian KB), known schema-screen interaction problem. (8) 'Two-week recovery rebuilding Slack and integrations' — universal post-migration cost. (9) 'Format conversion (Rally HTML rich text → Jira Wiki markdown)' — Rally→Jira specific (Ignite-Tec, Deviniti).
setup_praise: (1) 'Linear's bulk-delete-import lets us iterate fearlessly' — most-praised single migration feature in 2025 reviews. (2) 'Jira's new import experience auto-mapped 80% of my CSV columns' — Atlassian community 2024–2025. (3) 'OpsHub gave us zero-downtime Rally→ADO migration' — enterprise case studies. (4) 'Targetprocess CSV-via-ADM handled hierarchical backlogs with custom fields' — Targetprocess docs and case studies. (5) 'Notion's Monday importer brought boards over with structure intact' — Notion changelog 2025. (6) 'ServiceNow EAP-Jira OOTB integration finally available without custom scripting' — ServiceNow community Dec 2025. The praise patterns cluster around: visible auto-mapping, ability to undo, granular preview, and clear vendor support for the specific source-tool pair.
standout_setup_feature: Best-in-class single features across vendors: Linear — *bulk-delete-import* (one-click undo of an entire import) is the most user-empowering migration feature shipping today. Jira — *automatic CSV column-to-field name matching plus date-format detection* in the new import experience. Atlassian JCMA — *app assessment screen* that flags incompatible apps before migration (despite its UX flaws). OpsHub — *zero-downtime synchronization during cutover* for enterprise Rally migrations. Plane — *unified multi-source import UI* (Jira/Linear/Asana/ClickUp/Monday) in one wizard. ServiceNow EAP — *OOTB guided setup* shipped Dec 2025, removing the prior requirement for custom IntegrationHub work. The migration UX gold standard does not yet exist in any one product: it would combine Linear's undo + Jira's auto-mapping + OpsHub's zero-downtime + AI schema proposal + native sprint/history preservation.
servicenow_comparison: ServiceNow EAP's migration story has improved sharply with the Dec 2025 store release: the SPW Jira Integrations plugin ships an OOTB Jira integration with guided setup, removing prior custom-IntegrationHub work. The integration is positioned as a two-step interim approach, with a bidirectional native integration on the longer-term roadmap. Critical limitation: sprints cannot be synchronized in the interim approach — a meaningful gap when migrating active Jira teams. There is no shipped EAP equivalent to Linear's in-product importer for non-Jira sources (Asana, monday, Trello, CSV). Compared to Jira's new import experience (which absorbs migrations *from* Asana/monday/Linear/Trello/CSV), EAP's inbound migration surface is narrower. The strategic implication for AINPX: EAP's migration UX is the single biggest setup-time risk for enterprise prospects considering EAP over Jira Align or Planview Portfolios. Closing this gap with AI-assisted schema mapping, sprint-history preservation, and a Linear-style undo would be high-leverage. [uncertain] on whether sprint sync and broader source support is on the 2026 roadmap.
